messages:
maya: Hey folks — trying to use the JS SDK inside a Next.js middleware (edge runtime) and the Vercel build fails with: \"Module not found: Can't resolve 'stream'\" and later a \"ReferenceError: Buffer is not defined\". Anyone run into this?
simon: Which import are you using? top-level `import Redwood from 'redwood-inference'?`
maya: yep. Minimal example: ```js
import { client } from 'redwood-inference'
export function middleware(req) {
  return client.generate({ prompt: 'hi' })
}
``` Build fails only for middleware bundle (dev local server is fine).
eli: This is expected when the package pulls in node-only deps. The edge runtime doesn't have node core polyfills (stream, Buffer, fs, etc.). We publish an edge-friendly entrypoint — try `redwood-inference/edge`.
maya: Oh interesting, didn't see that in quickstart. Trying `import { createClient } from 'redwood-inference/edge'` now...
maya: OK build moved past the stream/Buffer error, but TypeScript in the middleware complains: \"Property 'signal' does not exist on type 'RequestInit'\" when we pass abort signals to fetch.
nicole: Next's middleware types are weird — they use a trimmed lib.dom. Two quick workarounds: 1) add the right libs in tsconfig (lib: ["DOM", "DOM.Iterable"]) or 2) cast to any for the call site. Neither is great. We should document the typing footguns.
simon: Another pattern is a dynamic import inside the handler: `const { createClient } = await import('redwood-inference/edge')`. That keeps the edge-safe codepath but avoids bundling node shims. But note Vercel still statically analyzes imports so explicit /edge entrypoint is more reliable.
maya: After switching to the /edge entrypoint the build passed. At runtime though I hit `TypeError: request.body.getReader is not a function` when the SDK tries to stream the user request body.
eli: Right — Next edge Request body shapes differ a bit. SDK was assuming a web ReadableStream with getReader. We'll add a tiny adapter: if `request.body?.getReader` is missing, fall back to `request.arrayBuffer()` or `request.text()` and create a small ReadableStream wrapper.
simon: Filed a small DX issue to cover this plus a sample middleware template: https://go/redwood/dx/456 (notes: /edge import, avoid Buffer/crypto.randomBytes, prefer global fetch/AbortController).
deploy-bot: Deployed branch `sdk/edge-adapter` -> staging at 2024-11-06T14:22Z :rocket:
maya: Nice — after the adapter patch runtime streaming works. One last ask: can we add a clear note in onboarding quickstart about edge runtime constraints (no fs, no node crypto, no Buffer, minimal typings) and a copy-paste middleware example?
nicole: Yep, I'll add a short \"Using Redwood SDK in Next middleware (Edge)\" section and link the sample repo. Also will add an explicit /edge entrypoint mention in CHANGELOG and the README.
maya: Thanks all! saved me a bunch of time :thumbsup:
eli: I'll add a small test matrix for Vercel Edge + Next middleware in CI so we don't regress.
simon: We should also add a lint rule to warn if top-level import from the main package is used in files under `middleware`/`app/middleware`. Could be a codemod later.
nicole: love that. sgtm.
